analysis:
Compared all supplied BASE/HEAD desktop workflow source. .github/workflows/release-desktop.yml changes only the source and publish runners to ubuntu-24.04 (HEAD 59, 519). The source gate still checks out master before verification (69–81); subsequent jobs use its source SHA. Signing/notarization remain on unchanged macOS runners, with separate dependency execution, bounded credential exposure, and package/signature checks. Publication still requires the source publish verdict (518), downloads by artifact ID/digest and checks SHA256SUMS (533–544), and uploads update metadata after packages (579–582). No supported regression in artifact trust, credentials, authorization or availability follows from these two runner substitutions. Relevant model contracts include A-011/A-017 and T-013/T-054; publication is not itself serving qualification. No inference encryption, cache isolation (T-041), billing or provider grant behavior changes are visible here.
Examined release-dev-branch.yml metadata and its supplied partial patch. The visible comments describe replacing push-triggered releases with scheduled/manual coalescing and default-branch dispatch to dev, which may affect release authorization and availability. Its extensive changed ranges include HEAD 55–171, but executable workflow changes are not supplied: the patch ends during introductory comments. Integration must inspect the full BASE/HEAD workflow and reconcile scheduled dispatch permissions, ref/source binding, change-detection and last-green-run logic, concurrency, and its call into release-provider.yml's source gate (A-017, T-054, A-018). Neither the comments nor missing implementation establish a vulnerability or safety; this material coverage limit requires deeper review. Helper implementations referenced by the unchanged desktop workflow were not examined.
